name: Elnath
description: A naked-eye star 41.1 parsecs away, 5.5 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 35497: radius 5.47 +/- 0.24 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.239 +/- 0.052 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 35497: effective temperature 12026 +/- 262 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

gravity.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 35497: log g 3.63, from Allende Prieto & Lambert (1999), as the paper lists it beside the diameter (Table 4)

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331, XHIP, HIP 25428: RV 9.2 +/- 2.5 km/s (quality A)

distance.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 35497: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 24.36 +/- 0.34 mas, inverted

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: A naked-eye star 41 parsecs away whose disc the NPOI measured: 5.5 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1.239 milliarcseconds, which gives 5.47 solar radii and 12,026 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 35497: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff
